narrative.text: Theron and Kaspar enter your office looking grim. Kaspar is holding a vial of penicillin and a lab report. Theron is holding an arrest warrant.

Chancellor, the state hospital supply chain has been compromised. The penicillin being distributed to the Kravenstal clinics is diluted. It's been cut with a useless filler to maximize profit. 12 patients have died from treatable infections because the drug was too weak to save them.

I traced the supply contract. The company providing the medicine is a shell corporation, and the majority shareholder is Bishop Viktor Renek — the Archbishop's cousin. The dilution is his profit margin. Twelve patients took that margin into their veins.

These vials didn't come from my laboratory. The state lab has made eleven million clean doses since week sixty-four. The north still buys through contractors, because we couldn't build a second line fast enough. This is the contractor.
We are still paying the cartel price for the clean stock in Ashenmere, Chancellor. The north got the cheap contract. This is what the cheap contract looks like.
After week sixty-four the clinics bought penicillin from anyone who would sell it. This is who sold it. I warned you then. I'm not saying it to be right. I'm saying it so that it goes in the minutes.

Renek's cousin. Diluting medicine. Killing patients. If I arrest him, it will be a massive blow to the Church. Renek will see it as a political attack on his family, and the Halvekist base will riot. But if I let him walk, I am complicit in murder. 12 people are dead. I cannot let that stand, no matter the political cost.

choices.text: Arrest the cousin and seize the company. The law applies to everyone.
Quietly force the cousin to flee the country. Avoid the scandal.
Use Krel to have the cousin assassinated. Make it look like a suicide.

narrative.text: Renek's cousin is taken from his office at 2pm. His lawyers file for release within the hour. They do not get it. The Archbishop issues a statement calling the arrest 'political persecution of a faithful servant.' Kaspar holds a press conference with the lab results and the twelve names. The Archbishop does not issue a second statement. The supply contract is cancelled; emergency stock arrives from the Orythian aid reserves within the week. Theron is calm for the first time in months. Kaspar is not calm. She goes back to work.

Krel delivers the message on a Tuesday. By Thursday, Renek's cousin has boarded a ferry to Lytheira with two suitcases and no public statement. The shell company is dissolved. A new supply contract is issued. The twelve deaths are recorded in the Ministry files as resulting from 'substandard imported pharmaceutical stock' — accurate, precise, and attributing the cause to no one living. Kaspar signs the incident report without looking at me.

The inquest finds cardiac arrest. He was 58 and in poor health, which is true — Krel researches these things. The supply contract is terminated the same day for 'administrative reasons.' A new contract is issued within the week. The Archbishop sends flowers to the family and a letter to my office expressing gratitude for my 'pastoral sensitivity' during a difficult time. I do not respond. Kaspar never asks what happened. Either she knows, or she has decided not to.
